ai-at-work.title: AI automation startup Relay shuts down, staff joins Google’s Chrome team
ai-at-work.excerpt: "We have some really ambitious plans to help you work with AI in Chrome to get things done, and I’ll have more to share soon," Jacob Bank, Relay founder and CEO, said.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Relay, an AI automation startup, shut down and its team got absorbed into Google's Chrome division. This matters because it signals how big tech is consolidating AI tooling directly into browsers rather than betting on standalone automation platforms, which means your enterprise AI strategy needs to account for Chrome-native capabilities becoming standard. Honestly, this is probably good news for companies tired of managing seventeen different automation tools, though it does mean Google just got a little more control over how millions of people work.

ai-at-work.title: Groq raises $350M to fuel its pivot from AI chips to neocloud
ai-at-work.excerpt: Groq raised $350 million at a $3.5 billion valuation as the former AI chipmaker pivots to a neocloud business and expands its Nvidia-powered data center footprint.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Groq just scored a massive $350 million funding round at a $3.5 billion valuation and is switching from making AI chips to running a cloud infrastructure business powered by Nvidia hardware. This matters to DWP pros because it signals where serious compute infrastructure money is flowing, and if your organization is evaluating AI tools or infrastructure partners, you need to watch who's actually backing the horses in this race. Honestly, watching a company raise this much cash to basically become a cloud reseller of someone else's chips is peak 2024 startup theater, but the real story is that enterprise AI infrastructure is consolidating fast.

ai-at-work.dwp_take: Anthropic just dropped Cowork, an AI agent for Claude Desktop that lets regular people automate file-based tasks without writing code. The kicker: they built the whole thing in ten days using Claude itself, which is either brilliant dogfooding or a sign that nobody really knows what they're doing yet.

tools-tech.title: Business adoption of AI agents tripled this year - as measurable ROI emerges
tools-tech.excerpt: Industries are finding the strategies that work best for their business needs, according to Salesforce's latest Agentic Enterprise Index.
tools-tech.dwp_take: Companies tripled their adoption of AI agents this year as they figured out which use cases actually deliver measurable returns instead of just chasing shiny objects. This matters to us digital workplace folks because AI agents are moving from "nice to have" curiosity projects into the actual tools we're deploying into everyday work, which means we need to stop theorizing and start getting practical about integration, governance, and user adoption. The real test isn't whether AI agents work—it's whether your organization can actually get people to use them without creating three new shadow systems in the process.

tools-tech.title: Google wants you to use its phones less and its AI more - but who's buying it?
tools-tech.excerpt: Google is leveraging our poor relationship to technology to sell its new phones - the same relationship it had a hand in creating.
tools-tech.dwp_take: Google is positioning its new phones as tools for reducing phone dependency while simultaneously promoting heavier AI usage instead. Digital workplace pros need to understand this shift because it signals how major tech vendors are reshaping productivity narratives around AI integration rather than genuine wellbeing. Here's the thing though: telling people to use your device less while asking them to use your AI more is like a casino saying they care about your gambling habits.

tools-tech.title: Google Workspace lets Gemini access your company data by default - how to shut it down
tools-tech.excerpt: In Google Workspace, Gemini has access to Gmail, Docs, Calendar, Chat, and more by default. Here's why it matters, and how administrators can disable it today.
tools-tech.dwp_take: Google shipped Gemini with access to your company's email, documents, calendar, and chat data turned on by default, leaving it to admins to opt out rather than opt in. This matters because most organizations won't catch this until someone asks why their confidential files are being fed into an AI model, and by then the damage is already done. Google's move here is the digital workplace equivalent of leaving your office door unlocked and handing the keys to whoever walks by, then acting surprised when people get upset.

tools-tech.title: AI inference is getting cheaper, but your agents are getting more expensive
tools-tech.excerpt: The good news is that large language model (LLM) token costs are coming down. The conundrum: The overall cost of AI workloads is going up. Gartner research predicts that, while token costs will fall b
tools-tech.dwp_take: The cost of individual AI tokens keeps dropping, but the total spend on AI agent workflows is climbing fast because developers are using way more tokens per task. This directly hits digital workplace budgets and ROI calculations for things like chatbots, automation, and knowledge work tools. So yeah, your boss will love hearing that token prices fell while your actual AI bill tripled, which is basically the tech equivalent of getting a discount on gas while buying a bigger truck.

digital-culture.dwp_take: A founder measured their brain activity during a brutal 10-day business trip across three countries and discovered that their packed schedule was actually tanking their cognitive performance, not boosting it. This matters because we've built entire workplace cultures around grinding through exhaustion, and neuroscience is finally giving us permission to call that what it is: stupid. The irony is thick here: the guy tracking his brain's performance probably would have performed better if he'd just taken a nap instead of wearing fancy headphones to prove he was falling apart.

Here's the thing though: if we've learned anything from the last few years, it's that introversion isn't a career limitation anymore, it's just a preference about how you work best, and that's worth accommodating whether you're running your own show or working for someone else.
